source.reason: The Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy was deformed by hot torsion in the temperature range 900–1100 °C with strain rates 0.1–10 s^-1.

processing_steps_notes.value: Strain rate range 0.1–10 s^-1. Hot deformation triggers dynamic recrystallization: DDRX at high temperature/high strain rate, CDRX at lower temperature/low strain rate.

source.reason: Recrystallization behavior of the ferritic Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy during hot torsion is described in the text and Fig. 6.

overall_structure.value: Ferritic Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy undergoing dynamic recrystallization during hot torsion: discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX) at high temperature/high strain rate and continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) at lower temperature/low strain rate.

source.reason: The recrystallization microstructure of the Fe-8 wt.% Al ferritic alloy under hot torsion is described via the DDRX/CDRX mechanisms.
The alloy is identified as a ferritic Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy (ferrite matrix).
Hot torsion tests were used to investigate dynamic recrystallization mechanisms in the Fe-8 wt.% Al ferritic alloy.

measurement_conditions.value: Temperature range 900–1100 °C; strain rate range 0.1–10 s^-1

purpose.value: Study effects of strain, strain rate, and temperature on dynamic recrystallization of the ferritic Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy

key_findings.value: DDRX at high temperature/high strain rate; CDRX at lower temperature/low strain rate

source.reason: Fig. 6 displays the strain rate–temperature map for DDRX activation in the Fe-8% Al ferritic steel.

technique.value: strain rate–temperature processing map (DDRX activation domain)

purpose.value: Map the activation domain of DDRX in the Fe-8% Al ferritic steel

key_findings.value: DDRX activated at high strain rate; not activated at low strain rate; critical strain rate boundary decreases as temperature rises (from between 1 and 10 s^-1 at 850 °C to just above 0.1 s^-1 at ~1150 °C); data columns at 900, 1000, 1100 °C.

unmapped_findings: Ferritic Fe-Al alloys often exhibit surface defects referred to as roping after deep drawing, mainly attributed to the inhomogeneous orientation distribution of individual grains; promoting a recrystallized structure by DDRX seems advantageous to limit roping (b0036, b0038).
Depending on the deformation conditions, there is a competition between DDRX and CDRX in the Fe-8 wt.% Al ferritic alloy (b0038).

The DDRX activation domain in the Fe-8% Al ferritic steel is delimited by a critical strain rate that decreases as temperature rises; experimental points lie in three vertical columns at 900, 1000 and 1100 °C (figure_006).
